instructions_en: Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Describe yourself as you honestly see yourself, in relation to other people you know of the same sex as you are, and roughly your same age. So that you can describe yourself in an honest manner, your responses will be kept in absolute confidence. Indicate for each statement whether it is 1. Very Inaccurate, 2. Moderately Inaccurate, 3. Neither Accurate Nor Inaccurate, 4. Moderately Accurate, or 5. Very Accurate as a description of you.

scoring.facet: sum of 4 items after reversing '-' keyed items; range 4-20
scoring.note: IPIP scoring instructions: assign 1-5 (Very Inaccurate..Very Accurate) to '+' items and 5-1 to '-' items, then sum. Mean scores (sum/number of items) are an equivalent alternative.

notes: Parsed 30 facets x 4 items = 120 from 30FacetNEO-PI-RItems.htm; 51 key blocks (26 '+' keyed, 25 '- keyed') as on the page.
Every item's facet and +/- key matches the IPIP-NEO-300 key (newNEOKey.htm).

Korean: 119 items matched by exact normalized English text shown next to the Korean on KoreanIPIP-NEO-300.htm; 1 matched manually (O6 'Believe that there is no absolute right and wrong.' - page has 'right or wrong').
The Korean page lists the 300 items in the IPIP-NEO-300 round-robin facet order (checked: every row's facet follows N1,E1,O1,A1,C1,N2,... repeating), so row number = IPIP-NEO-300 item position.
English kept exactly as on the 120-item page, including 'right and wrong' for the O6 item.
Administration order: round robin over N1,E1,O1,A1,C1,...,N6,E6,O6,A6,C6, 4 passes, items in listed order within facet (order = pass*30 + facet position + 1).

9 items have ko_note/ko_alt because the official Korean drifts in meaning; 'ko' always holds the official source text, 'ko_alt' is a suggested replacement (self_translated_unverified unless ko_alt_source says otherwise).
Facet Korean names are chosen by the builder (based on usual Korean NEO-PI-R naming); IPIP facet labels differ from NEO-PI-R in places (e.g., N5 Immoderation vs Impulsiveness).
